title: Opt-in Rollforward and Evidence Kit — Tenant Choice Guide (draft)
body:
TL;DR

This doc is a customer-facing draft that gives tenants three clear, actionable choices after the inference disruption on 2029-11-28: 1) opt in to a controlled rollforward (replay) to regenerate affected responses, 2) request an evidence package to independently verify integrity without replaying, or 3) decline automated remediation and keep current records. Each choice includes concise next steps, expected outcomes, and timelines.

Audience and intent
- Audience: tenant technical leads, engineering contacts, and integration owners who observed inconsistent outputs during the incident.
- Intent: present transparent options and self-service instructions so customers can choose the remediation path that best fits their compliance/consistency needs.
- Tone: factual, neutral, actionable, low-legalese, with clear verification checkpoints.

Background (one-paragraph summary)
On 2029-11-28 at ~02:07 UTC, a deployment pipeline change caused an inconsistent kernel selection path in the serving runtime for a subset of model variants. This produced nondeterministic responses for requests meeting a specific token-length and quantization profile. The issue affected approximately 1.2% of requests within the EU region between 02:07–03:10 UTC. Full technical RCA is being finalized in OPS-1342; the purpose of this note is to present remediation choices to tenants and the evidence we can provide.

Scope and who was affected
- Affected tenants: tenants with active EU-region endpoints using model family rwd-v2.* with dynamic quantization enabled.
- Visible symptoms for tenants: occasional truncated or semantically inconsistent completions, higher-than-normal variance in embeddings for identical inputs, and—rarely—partial stream interruptions.
- Non-impacted: private deployments (VPC/on-prem) that did not pull the affected runtime image, and requests routed to dedicated reserved capacity that used pinned kernels.

What we did to contain the problem (brief)
- Immediately rolled service routing to fallback kernel selection for all EU endpoints at 03:12 UTC.
- Disabled the pipeline change and reverted to the last verified runtime image at 03:27 UTC.
- Launched an audit job to identify impacted request ids and collect deterministic evidence artifacts (request/response digests, KV-cache snapshots, runtime logs).

Remediation options for tenants (clear choices)
Option A — Opt-in Rollforward (replay and regenerate outputs)
- What it is: We re-execute affected requests on the verified runtime image and produce regenerated outputs under controlled conditions.
- Who should choose this: tenants that require corrected outputs in upstream systems (search indexes, user-visible content) and have automated consumers that can accept regenerated responses.
- How it works: tenants supply the tenancy ID(s) to opt-in (or we use tenancy-scoped filter if they already consented in the console). We then re-run requests in chronological order preserving original request metadata (prompt, system messages, temperature, max_tokens). We tag regenerated responses with an audit header and store both original and regenerated artifacts in the evidence package.
- Expected outcomes and timeline: bulk replays are rate-limited to avoid cross-tenant interference. Small tenants (<= 1M tokens affected) see results within 6–12 hours; larger tenants may take 24–72 hours.
- Risks/notes: regenerated outputs may differ in wording from originals—this is expected when nondeterminism exists. We provide a diff/side-by-side viewer and confidence metrics to help decide acceptance.

Option B — Evidence Package (no replay)
- What it is: We provide a signed evidence bundle per tenant that contains cryptographic digests of original inputs/outputs, runtime logs, shard-level KV-cache snapshots, and checksums so tenants can independently verify whether their data was mutated or truncated.
- Who should choose this: tenants with strict audit/regulatory requirements who prefer an independent verification rather than regenerated content.
- How it works: tenant requests an evidence package via support portal or the console. We produce a tamper-evident archive with: request ids, timestamps, raw response blobs, SHA-256 digests, server-side logs, and a short runbook describing how to verify. Archive includes a short integrity verification script and a signed manifest.
- Expected outcomes and timeline: evidence package delivery within 12–36 hours depending on affected volume.

Option C — No Automated Change (retain current records)
- What it is: Tenants elect to keep existing stored responses as-is and decline both replay and evidence bundling at this time.
- Who should choose this: tenants that have downstream systems where historical fidelity must be preserved (e.g., legal records) and prefer not to alter previously stored data.
- How it works: Tenant notifies account contact or selects the console opt-out. We mark the tenant record as 'no-change' and stop automated remediation for their tenant id.

How to choose and next steps (practical guide)
1) Quick self-assessment questions for tenant teams:
   - Are affected responses user-visible or archived as part of a regulated record? If yes, consider Option B or C.
   - Can you tolerate regenerated outputs with potential wording differences? If yes, Option A is likely preferred.
   - Do you need deterministic embeddings for downstream vectors stores? If yes, Option B is recommended so you can verify integrity before deciding.
2) How to request an option: console (Recommended): Settings → Tenancy → Incident actions → "Opt-in rollforward / Evidence kit"; Support: open ticket referencing JIRA-OPS-1342 and include tenant id; API: POST /v1/tenancies/{id}/incident-actions (beta) with body {"action": "rollforward" | "evidence" | "no_change"}.
3) Required tenant inputs for rollforward: tenancy id, minimum residency window (start/end timestamps), and whether to accept regenerated outputs automatically or queue for review.

Verification artifacts we will provide (standardized)
- Request/response pairs (original and regenerated where applicable)
- SHA-256 digests and signed manifest (to check artifact integrity)
- Runtime logs keyed to request id and worker id (redacted for internal IPs)
- KV-cache snapshots: sequence window covering the affected request lifetime
- Side-by-side diff report with token-level alignment and a simple scoring metric that approximates semantic parity

Security and privacy notes
- We will only include tenant-scoped data in evidence packages. No cross-tenant data will be shared.
- Sensitive fields already redacted by tenant-side masking are kept redacted.
- Evidence archives are delivered via a short-lived, authenticated S3 link (or via secure transfer on request) and are signed by Redwood's incident signing key.

Compensation and credits
- We are offering a one-time service credit proportional to affected tokens for tenants that choose Option A or B. Support will append a credit note to the tenant billing account after remediation completes. Exact credit amounts and thresholds are provided in the Support UI when selecting an option.

Example timelines and SLAs
- Acknowledgement: within 4 business hours of a request.
- Evidence delivery: 12–36 hours.
- Rollforward completion (<=1M tokens): 6–12 hours; >1M tokens: 24–72 hours.
- Post-replay follow-up: 3 business days for questions or appeals.

Customer-facing FAQ (short answers)
Q: Will regenerated outputs be identical to originals?
A: Not guaranteed—regenerated outputs may differ in phrasing. We provide side-by-side diffs and a semantic parity score to help decide if you accept regenerated responses.

Q: Can you replay only a subset of requests?
A: Yes. You can supply filters (time ranges, request ids, or API keys) when opting in.

Q: Is there risk to my downstream systems during replay?
A: Replays are rate-limited and can be executed to a separate bucket to avoid overwriting live downstream data unless you explicitly choose automatic replacement.

Q: How do you guarantee evidence integrity?
A: Artifacts are bundled with SHA-256 digests, a signed manifest, and our incident signing key that you can validate independently.

Contacts and escalation
- Primary incident contact: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai)
- Support intake: support@redwood.ai (include tenancy id and OPS-1342 in subject)
- Enterprise escalation: Priya Nair (enterprise-success@redwood.ai)

Appendix: minimal example console text for tenants
Header: "2029-11-28 Runtime Inconsistency — Choose a remediation path"
Body: "We detected inconsistent outputs for a subset of requests. Choose: 1) \"Regenerate responses (rollforward)\" — we will re-run your affected requests on the verified runtime and provide side-by-side diffs; 2) \"Request evidence package\" — receive a tamper-evident archive of original artifacts; 3) \"No change\" — we will not alter historical records. Clicklearn more"

Open questions for internal review (for CS + Ops)
- Finalize credit calculation thresholds.
- Confirm exact naming for the signed manifest and incident signing key handling.
- Decide whether rollforward auto-replacement requires explicit separate opt-in for tenants with archival retention policies.

Draft status and next internal steps
- This draft is intended for legal and ops review before we publish on the status page and enable console actions.
- Action owners: Ops (Ibrahim) to finalize artifact export paths; SRE (Evan) to confirm replay throttle; Legal (Sofia) to review wording and credits language.
